# Minimum Changes To Make Alternating Binary String.

@example Changing the first digit gives "10101".
"00101"
=> 1

@example Changing the second and the fifth digit gives "101010"; the other alternating string, "010101", is 4 changes away.
"111000"
=> 2

@example No two neighbours are equal, so no change is needed.
"10101"
=> 0

# One character is always alternating.
"0"
=> 0

"1"
=> 0

# Two equal characters.
"11"
=> 1

# A pair of equal neighbours in the middle still costs 2: changing one of
# the 1s leaves another pair.
"0110"
=> 2

# All the same digit, odd and even lengths.
"1111111"
=> 3

"000000"
=> 3

# A long run inside: four pairs of equal neighbours, but 2 changes.
"1000001"
=> 2

# Runs of mixed lengths, two of them even: 6 changes.
"0100111010010"
=> 6

# Only the first digit is wrong: keeping it would cost 12 changes.
"1101010101010"
=> 1

# 300 ones then 300 zeros: an answer above 255.
""
=> 300

# 10^4 digits: the first one and three in every ten are wrong, 3001 in
# all; keeping the first digit would cost 6999.
""
=> 3001

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them). Full-size
# ones (10^4 digits) come with milestone M7.
@gen 1 small
"001"
=> 1

@gen 2 small
"00000"
=> 2

@gen 3 small
"000100001100"
=> 5

@gen 4 small
"10001100"
=> 3

@gen 5 small
"1100101011"
=> 3

@gen 6 small
"0100001001"
=> 4

@gen 7 small
"1100011100"
=> 4

@gen 8 small
"111"
=> 1
